fixes.explanation: Yes, friend! "And the birds of prey descended on the carcasses, but Abram drove them away." (Genesis 15:11). So Abram doesn't hand them over. He steps in and shoos them off. I picture him waving his arms like I wave my mustache at a crumb thief.

Yes, friend! Abram says, "…a servant in my household will be my heir." (Genesis 15:3). I think he's laying out his problem for God. Then God answers, "This one will not be your heir, but one who comes from your own body will be your heir." (Genesis 15:4).

Sand is a good thought, baker, and you're in the right neighborhood. But the stars are what God names here. He says, "Now look to the heavens and count the stars, if you are able." (Genesis 15:5). Sand is down at your feet, and God has Abram looking up.

Flocks? I see you thinking like a man with a lot of sheep, friend. God never brings them up in this moment. He tells Abram, "Now look to the heavens and count the stars, if you are able." (Genesis 15:5). The words "if you are able" tell you this is a count Abram can't finish.

Tents, huh? Good guess for a man who lives in them, but God has something bigger in mind. He says, "Now look to the heavens and count the stars, if you are able." (Genesis 15:5). Abram has to leave the tent and go outside to see it, because the LORD "took him outside" first.
